gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-syriac-easter: Approachable and contemporary, Noto Sans Syriac Eastern keeps its tall lowercase well ahead of its small caps. Quilon is the showier one, with visible but mild stroke contrast, while the sans body simply gets on with the text.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-syriac-wester: Quilon's strokes swell and thin in a modest, steady rhythm, giving the display lettering an editorial pull. And Noto Sans Syriac Western answers it with small letters packed dense and tall, like bundled cable.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Quilon opens with commanding, editorial presence, its stroke modulation tempered and its big a, e and s wide open. Noto Sans Tagalog is the quiet one, its middle zone dominating each line.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Clean and modern, Noto Sans Tagbanwa fills most of the line height with lowercase and leaves clear gaps in every curve. Quilon heads it with thin strokes only slightly lighter than its thick ones, so a long page stays smooth and unhurried.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Quilon has a restful line, its stroke weight swinging only modestly, and the large open a, e and s give it an editorial voice. And Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its ink strokes out before they touch, a neutral partner for it.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Noto Sans Tai Viet pairs short ascenders with a tall x-height, and its terminals pull back from each curve's closing point. But shrink Quilon down and its visible, restrained thick-thin gap would soften, so it wants room.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri reads high-waisted and contemporary, with every small round letter left generously unclosed at the curve. Quilon, with its modest dip in the thin strokes, adds the commanding edge.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Big, bold, almost magnified: Noto Sans Tamil looks enlarged at any size, with terminals stopping far from the stem. Quilon thins out modestly where its curves turn; leave the body size generous.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tamil-supplem: Contemporary and clean, Noto Sans Tamil Supplement draws round forms like open parentheses inside a middle band so tall the line looks stocky. Quilon, with tempered modulation, feels more editorial beside it.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Quilon's calm ebb and flow of stroke thickness gives it an editorial, commanding stance, with a modest, readable weight shift across every curve. And Noto Sans Tangsa follows with wide, inviting round letters and short ascender stems, so paragraphs would move along comfortably.
